I migrated the file to es-toolkit and wrote it to `out/module.ts`. Type checking shows no errors for it. I didn't run the original against it to compare outputs, and lodash isn't installed here, so I couldn't measure the original's size either.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 636 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of my own code.

- **`doubled`:** uses `mapValues` from `es-toolkit`, with the same callback.
- **`byNameKey`:** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. es-toolkit's `keyBy` takes a function instead of lodash's `'name'` string shorthand, so the adapter is `(row) => row.name`.
- **`isBlank`:** uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The non-compat build has no general `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`, which doesn't cover null, strings, arrays or numbers. I read the compat source, and it follows lodash's rules for your input range. It treats null, booleans and numbers as empty. It treats a string, array or object as empty only when it has no characters, elements or keys.

No lodash import remains, and the exports (`Row`, `Config`, `doubled`, `byNameKey`, `isBlank`) are unchanged.
